question: Should OpenClaw adopt purpose-specific memory role slots as a core/plugin API now, using the linked implementation path after conflict repair, or keep the single memory slot and solve coexistence with narrower plugin-specific mechanisms?
rationale: This changes public config, plugin activation, per-agent behavior, docs, and upgrade semantics, while VISION.md gives mixed guidance: memory is currently a special single slot, but missing plugin API seams are welcome design-discussion territory.

options.title: Sponsor role slots
options.body: Review the API direction in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/88504, require conflict repair plus upgrade proof, and land if the public contract is accepted.

options.title: Narrow coexistence repairs
options.body: Keep the scalar memory slot and handle Honcho, dreaming, capture, and recall coexistence through targeted plugin/runtime hooks instead of a role-slot taxonomy.

options.title: Decline multi-slot core API
options.body: Close the architecture direction with a maintainer rationale and point affected providers to plugin-specific or ClawHub-owned integration patterns.

recommendation.title: Sponsor role slots
recommendation.body: Review the API direction in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/88504, require conflict repair plus upgrade proof, and land if the public contract is accepted.

likelyOwner.reason: The current scalar slot implementation blames to this handle and recent merged memory-loader work makes them the strongest routing candidate for the API/compatibility decision.
